questions.question: 1. Increasing the value of the variable width will:

answers.d: May improve or make worse depending on the interval

explanations.a: Incorrect. Increasing the width generally reduces accuracy.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Changing the width affects the approximation.
explanations.c: Correct. Increasing the width makes the approximation worse because fewer rectangles are used, so the fit is less accurate.
explanations.d: Incorrect. While the effect may vary, generally increasing width worsens the approximation.

questions.question: 2. Which method divides the interval into equal segments and uses the function value at the midpoint of each segment to estimate area?

explanations.a: Incorrect. The left endpoint rule uses the function value at the start of each segment.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The right endpoint rule uses the function value at the end of each segment.
explanations.c: Correct. The midpoint rule uses the function value at the midpoint of each segment.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The trapezoidal rule uses the average of the function values at the endpoints.

questions.question: 3. For which type of function does the rectangle approximation method give the exact area under the curve?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Linear functions may not always be exactly approximated unless the interval matches the slope.
explanations.b: Correct. For constant functions, the rectangle method gives the exact area.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Quadratic functions are not exactly approximated by rectangles.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Exponential functions are not exactly approximated by rectangles.

questions.question: 4. True or False: Numerical approximation methods can be used to estimate the area under any curve, regardless of whether the function is integrable analytically.

explanations.a: Correct. Numerical methods can estimate the area under any curve, even if the function cannot be integrated analytically.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Numerical methods are not limited by analytical integrability.
